subject: Territorial hosting provenance & private fabric checklist
messages:
From: julie.roman@medverahealth.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medverahealth.com; security@medverahealth.com
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: deployment provenance + private peering checklist

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team needs a concise provenance statement for the pilot: we need to show where request processing, model inference, KV/backups, and logs are hosted (region per workload), plus confirmation of private peering options (Privatelink/VPC peering) and KMS region residency.

Specifically MedVera is asking for:
- A one-page statement that we can include in our SIG/CAIQ submission showing all data-in-transit and at-rest residency for the pilot (processing vs backups).
- An ops checklist confirming private peering steps, IP ranges, and any fallback routing to public-hosted endpoints.
- The region(s) where customer-managed KMS keys can be configured and whether key material ever leaves those regions.

We have a tight compliance review window and would like artifacts by EOD Aug 18 if possible. Is that doable?

Best,
Julie Roman
Director, Security Engineering
MedVera Health
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: julie.roman@medverahealth.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 12 Aug 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance + private peering checklist

Hi Julie — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provide a concise provenance letter plus a private-fabric checklist and KMS region matrix by EOD 18th.

Plan:
1) I will draft a one-page "provenance statement" that maps request path -> compute region -> backing storage.
2) Irene will add the SOC 2 / CAIQ references and confirm any log-retention caveats.
3) Karthik will produce the privatelink/topology checklist with IP ranges and step-by-step ops actions (peering, route tables, SGs, and fallback rules).

Can you confirm the pilot account name we should reference (legal redaction requirements)? Also, do you need RPO/RTO numbers included?

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com; irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Request: deployment provenance + private peering checklist

FYI — forwarding to infra/ops for artifacts. Draft items I plan to attach:
- privatelink_topology_v2.png (diagram of peering endpoints, NAT/FW placement)
- kms-region-matrix.xlsx (which services/kms keys can be bound to which region)
- redwood_provenance_letter_v1.pdf (one-page statement draft)

Notes:
- For the hosted API (default): inference compute runs in the configured region and ephemeral caches live in that region for the request lifespan. Long-term backups (S3 snapshot store) are retained in the region specified on contract; by default our hosted EU offering snapshots to eu-west-1 unless otherwise requested.
- KMS: customer-managed keys are supported in US and EU regions; key material is never exported from the configured region — we use regional HSM/KMS partitions and cross-region replication is opt-in.

Action items for me: confirm exact IP CIDR blocks for Privatelink and provide a short ops runbook for failover to public endpoints (we keep a read-only fallback service).

—Karthik
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: julie.roman@medverahealth.com; stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: deployment provenance + private peering checklist

Hi Julie — attaching the compliance references you'll need for the SIG/CAIQ row mapping. A few clarifications up front:
- SOC 2: our current report (Type II) covers logical access, change management, and availability controls for hosted services; we will include the SOC 2 identifier in the provenance letter.
- CAIQ: we will supply the completed CAIQ rows relevant to Data Residency (IaaS boundaries), Crypto/KMS handling, and Network Controls (Privatelink).
- Logs: audit logs are stored in the same region as the compute by default; on request we can configure log export to a set region for longer retention.

I have flagged one operational caveat: if you request cross-region replication of backups for disaster recovery, that replication path will transfer snapshot data to the secondary region unless you opt for region-bound retention only. We will clearly call that out in the draft.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: julie.roman@medverahealth.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com; irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Provenance statement + private fabric checklist (MedVera pilot)

Julie — attaching the artifacts you requested. Summary below, attachments in Drive link and included files.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Inference and request processing: hosted in the region you select for the pilot (we default to us-west-2 for US pilots).
- Ephemeral caches / KV: strictly regional and scoped to the request lifetime; no cross-region cache replication in default config.
- Persistent backups / snapshots: retained in the configured region unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled (this is an opt-in DR feature).
- KMS: customer-managed keys can be provisioned in us-west-2 or eu-west-1; key material is bound to the selected KMS region and is not exported by Redwood.
- Private peering: Privatelink endpoints available in the selected region; we provide IP CIDR ranges and an ops checklist for route-table setup, SG rules, and failover to our read-only public endpoint if peering is not available.

Attachments included: redwood_provenance_letter_v1.pdf; privatelink_topology_v2.png; kms-region-matrix.xlsx
Drive pack: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/MedVera-Proofpack

Next steps: please confirm the pilot region and whether you want cross-region snapshot replication enabled; Karthik can schedule a short ops call to walk your infra team through Privatelink steps.

—Stephanie
From: julie.roman@medverahealth.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@medverahealth.com; security@medverahealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provenance statement + private fabric checklist (MedVera pilot)

Thanks — received and this looks good. A couple quick clarifications from security:
- Confirmed pilot region: us-west-2 (please reference in the provenance letter).
- We will not enable cross-region snapshot replication for the pilot (region-bound retention only).
- Can Karthik share the Privatelink CIDR and a short step-by-step for setting up route53 private zones during the ops call?

If everything is as stated, I'll mark the SIG response as complete and attach your provenance letter to the submission.

Julie
Director, Security Engineering, MedVera Health
